system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the belt tension-strain-fatigue relationship. Cover wear reduces the belt's cross-sectional area, increasing stress for the same tension. Carcass fatigue reduces the effective elastic modulus, increasing strain. Both effects increase drive-motor current for the same load, but at different rates. USER CONSTRAINT: 1-minute resolution data from existing sensors.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: Existing belt-scale (load measurement) and drive-motor current sensors. Processing: Time-series analysis software to calculate the load-normalized current (current/load ratio). Procedure: Continuously monitor the 1-minute average load and current. Calculate the moving average (7-day window) of the load-normalized current. Flag when this value exceeds baseline by 15% for 3 consecutive days. ASSUMPTION: Baseline established during normal operation.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Standard practice is periodic visual inspection, which has no predictive capability and requires conveyor downtime. This approach uses existing sensors with minimal added cost (software only). It provides early warning without downtime, but requires baseline calibration. Rough cost class: $0 in hardware, $5k-10k in software development/integration.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install monitoring system on 10 overland conveyors with known belt ages (2-5 years). Record load-normalized current continuously. Flag when threshold is exceeded. Instruments: Existing belt-scale and current sensors, data logging system. Pass/fail threshold: Must flag all belts that fail within 3 weeks, with no more than 2 false alarms per year across all 10 conveyors. Duration: 12 months of continuous monitoring. USER CONSTRAINT: 3-week warning before failure, 2 false alarms per year maximum.
